known_constraints.detail: Agent Engine deployed with enable_tracing=True under a service account holding roles/cloudtrace.agent produced no readable spans. cloudtrace.googleapis.com and telemetry.googleapis.com are both enabled, cloudtrace v1 traces.list returns 0 over a 3 hour window in COMPLETE and ROOTSPAN views, telemetry.googleapis.com exposes no v1 trace read path, and the engine logged no warning.
known_constraints.effect: ManagedPathReceipt reports managed_status UNAVAILABLE with reason trace_has_no_spans rather than claiming a healthy managed path
root_cause: write 1: passing enable_tracing to AdkApp at all, even as False, takes telemetry away from the environment variables. The runtime logs: remove the enable_tracing parameter from your deployment code.

write 2: opentelemetry-instrumentation-google-genai was not installed, so the model call produced no GenAI span at all. The runtime logs: telemetry enabled but proceeding without Google GenAI instrumentation.
write 3: the service account lacked roles/monitoring.metricWriter, so the runtime logged Failed to export metrics batch code: 403.
read: Cloud Trace v1 projects.traces.list returns 0 even for a trace that projects.traces.get returns, so search is not a usable lookup path.

propagation: the managed runtime terminates the caller request at the API frontend and makes its own internal call (POST /api/stream_reasoning_engine), so a traceparent sent to :streamQuery does not reach the agent container.
fix: the caller mints the 32 hex trace id, injects it as a W3C traceparent on the :streamQuery call, and reads it back with projects.traces.get
known_constraints.privacy_note: OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT is deliberately left unset and ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS is false, because those switches put prompt and response text into spans and the artifact contracts forbid raw sensitive text in cloud artifacts
known_constraints.resolution: The Controller mints the trace id, records a root span for the run and one child span per agent call it actually made, writes them with cloudtrace v2 traces:batchWrite, and reads them back with v1 traces.get.
known_constraints.verified: 2026-08-22T19:38Z trace 2 spans read back, managed_status MANAGED, receipt status VALID

known_constraints.detail: When the gcloud CLI credential expires it waits on an interactive reauth prompt that never arrives. Scripts now cap every gcloud call and infra/smoke/env.sh reads the project from the gcloud configuration file instead of calling `gcloud config get-value`.

A failed getIamPolicy returns an error document. Merging grants into that and writing it back would have deleted every binding on the project; the write was only rejected because the Cloud Resource Manager API was disabled.
known_constraints.mitigation: parse_policy_document rejects error bodies, empty binding lists and missing etags; assert_additive_policy_write refuses any write that drops an existing grant or carries a changed etag. Both are covered by tests in tests/platform/test_iam_policy_guard.py.

known_constraints.detail: The project virtualenv lost every .py file under google/protobuf while dist-info still reported protobuf 7.36.0, which broke test collection. Repaired with an in-place reinstall of the same version; pyproject.toml and uv.lock were not touched.

tool_gateway.why: agent tools must not hold data-store access. The Assessor and Auditor accounts have no Firestore role by design and only the Controller writes the ledger, so tools call an authenticated internal Controller endpoint that authorises, records a receipt, invokes the real connector or ledger port, and returns a bounded result.
tool_gateway.architecture_decision: separate service rather than folded into a Controller service, because zero Cloud Run services exist in the project: there is no Controller service to host it. Measured 2026-08-24, run.services returned 0.
tool_gateway.controller_keeps: roles/datastore.user; no agent account gains it
tool_gateway.blocked_on: the agents lane endpoint contract and asset manifest, plus the container image reference. Deployment requirements are read from that file; nothing is inferred.
verify_fails_on: any allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers binding on any role

concurrency.evidence: FirestoreGatewayInvocationStore.reserve and .complete both run under @firestore.transactional against a document keyed by request_id in the tool_gateway_invocations collection, so the reservation is persisted shared state rather than per-process memory
concurrency.instance_scaling: unconstrained; no max-instances cap is required for correctness
concurrency.workers_rationale: throughput only: the bounded backends gain nothing from in-process concurrency. Correctness does not depend on the worker count.
concurrency.determined: 2026-08-24, read from the store implementation rather than assumed
